clue.text: Merchant's parent company quietly invested in chocolate

indicators.note: money invested in a fund disappears inside it, and these letters go the same way

blocks.note: ma is the everyday word for a mother
a Rolo is a chocolate, and it opens up after its first letter
CO is the abbreviation on a firm's letterhead
p is piano in music, the mark telling a player to be quiet

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sells you a corporate story of parents and investments, while the wordplay wants only a mother, a firm and a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo traded along the Silk Road for his family firm, so 'Merchant' defines by example, one trader standing for the name.

clue.text: Greek character vocalises thoughts

blocks.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
to vocalise a tune is to sing it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' is a letter of the alphabet, not somebody from Athens, and that swap is the whole of the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Musings are the reflections you turn over idly, so the plural noun steps straight into the place of 'thoughts'.

clue.text: Command doctor to check king's file before operation's conclusion

indicators.note: to check a thing is to hold it in, and whatever is held in ends up inside
what comes before something takes the earlier place, so the built-up chunk leads

blocks.note: to doctor a result is to rig it
in chess the king starts on e1, so the e-file is his
the letter operatioN concludes on

explanation.walkthrough: Two hospital words are doing other jobs: the doctor is a verb meaning to fiddle with, and the file is a chessboard's rather than a patient's.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold sway over a country, which is 'Command' in its royal sense rather than its military one.

clue.text: Palaeontologist dismissing Newton must pay

indicators.note: to dismiss somebody is to send them off the premises, and the letter named leaves the same way

blocks.note: the Victorian naturalist who coined the word 'dinosaur' has this surname
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.walkthrough: One scientist gives up a letter to another: the man supplies the word and the unit of force takes its symbol back out.
explanation.definitionFit: If you owe, a payment is due from you, so 'must pay' is the obligation the verb carries rather than the act itself.

clue.text: Pretended back in Tokyo Biles managed to claim perfect scores

indicators.note: the back of a word is the letter standing at its rear
a managed thing has been arranged to suit whoever ran it, letters included
to claim something is to take hold of it, so it finishes up gripped inside

blocks.note: the letter at TokyO's back
the gymnast's five letters are the fodder, and they resettle as S ... IBLE
a perfect score in gymnastics is a ten, and more than one makes tens

explanation.walkthrough: Simone Biles at the Tokyo Olympics is the picture the clue paints; the wordplay wants her surname's letters and the marks she was given.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ostensible is so only in appearance, which is what a pretended reason is - the adjective for a show put on.

clue.text: Pass with third in Geography at Cambridge University

indicators.note: counting in from the front of a word, the third one along is the letter wanted

blocks.note: geOgraphy, counted in three letters
MIT is the university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.walkthrough: The Cambridge the surface offers is the English one with the third-class degrees; the wordplay means the other one, across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to pass over it and leave it out - 'pass' in the sense of skipping a turn, not of succeeding.

clue.text: Chipmunk back to irk exterminator?

indicators.note: the back of a word is the letter at its rear, the last one you write

blocks.note: Chip and Dale are Disney's chipmunks, and this is the second of the pair
the letter standing at the back of irK

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is doing real work: these creatures exterminate nobody by trade, they simply shriek the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalek's one line is 'Exterminate!', so the clue names the creature by the threat it screeches rather than by what it is.

clue.text: Death that is going without international uproar

indicators.note: to go without a thing is to manage with it absent, so the letter named is simply not there

blocks.note: id est is Latin for 'that is', the phrase behind i.e.
I is the abbreviation for international, and it is the letter that goes
a ruction is a noisy row

explanation.walkthrough: Latin is the key here: read 'that is' as id est rather than as plain English, and the letter to be dropped has somewhere to come from.
explanation.definitionFit: The destruction of a thing is its end, and death is the end of a living one - the same noun used of buildings, forests and armies.

clue.text: Removing church influence from new Sicilian government

indicators.note: something made new is not the shape it used to be, and neither are these letters

blocks.note: eight letters from the island's adjective
G is government in the abbreviations, the ninth letter needed

explanation.walkthrough: Mafia politics is the picture, but 'new' is doing nothing more sinister than telling you the letters will not stay where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: To laicise is to hand a school or an office from the clergy to lay people, which is exactly removing the church's influence.

clue.text: Descriptor of island population left abandoned

blocks.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
the world means the people in it - 'the whole world knows'
L is left, and it is the letter that is dropped

explanation.walkthrough: Both nouns are in disguise: an island that is never called an island, and a population read as the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyword is the term chosen to describe or index a thing, so 'Descriptor' is the librarian's name for the job it does.

clue.text: Gooey substance produced by small tree

blocks.note: S is the label sewn into the smallest size
the lime is a common street tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced by' is only joinery: nothing is being manufactured, the two pieces simply sit end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is the thick sticky stuff a snail leaves behind it, which is the gooey substance wanted.

clue.text: New hairstylist cutting as intensely

indicators.note: made new means made over, and letters made over do not keep the order they came in
to cut a thing is to take it out, so those letters never reach the answer

blocks.note: eleven letters to start from
the two letters cut away, leaving the nine wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The salon picture holds together because cutting is what stylists do - and it is also the instruction to lose two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink or read something thirstily is to do it with a parched eagerness, so the adverb carries intensity rather than thirst.

clue.text: Buff relative given piercing

blocks.note: nan is what a great many people call their grandmother
a keen wind is a piercing one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' is neither the enthusiast nor the bare skin here but a colour, which is the last of its senses most solvers reach for.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth from Nanking, and the pale brownish-yellow it comes in is the shade called buff.

clue.text: Anticipate talk to get something off your chest?

blocks.note: to expect a thing is to anticipate it
to orate is to talk at length in public

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the joke: the idiom means unburdening yourself of a secret, and the medical sense means clearing the chest quite literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to cough phlegm up out of the chest, so the idiom for confessing is being read at its physical value.

clue.text: Play duke wrong wearing gold ring

indicators.note: what you wear goes round you, so the piece doing the wearing sits inside its clothes

blocks.note: or is gold on a coat of arms
a wrong done is a sin
a ring is a circle, written as the letter O

explanation.walkthrough: Two conventions worth banking for good: OR is gold in heraldry, and a ring is always the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the lovesick duke who opens Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, so the clue defines by example - one duke standing for the name.

clue.text: Saw her cavorting with 5 in addition

indicators.note: letters cavorting are letters skipping about, and they do not land back where they started

blocks.note: six letters to start from
the answer at 5 down joins in, four letters more

explanation.walkthrough: A number in a clue points at another entry: solve 5 down first and its four letters become part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What is more' is the phrase you tack on ahead of an extra point, which is the job 'in addition' does in a sentence.

clue.text: Make love to wife on vacation - it helps to exercise

indicators.note: a house whose occupants are on vacation stands empty in the middle, and so does the word
to exercise a thing is to put it through its paces, and letters put through theirs come out in a new order

blocks.note: wife with its insides away leaves the two outer letters
seven letters more, which with the WE make the nine wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes the second half look like a remark about the first; it is really the fodder and the instruction to shuffle it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep with someone is the polite English idiom for going to bed with them, which is what 'make love to' says outright.

clue.text: English theatre production's ending with Herod falsely made king

indicators.note: the ending of a word is the letter it stops on
a false version of a thing has its parts in the wrong places, letters included

blocks.note: E is English in the abbreviations
the NT is the National Theatre on the South Bank
the king of the nativity story, five letters of fodder
the letter productioN ends on, joining the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: Herod stands in the surface as a stage villain and in the wordplay as five loose letters - and the definition is what Rome did to him.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enthroned is to be set on the throne, and setting somebody on a throne is what making them king consists of.

clue.text: Youngster disheartened having lost clothing in luggage

indicators.note: what has been lost is not there any more, so those letters never reach the answer
clothes go on the outside, so the clothing of a word is the letter standing at each of its ends

blocks.note: to be chilled is to be dispirited, and these seven letters are the word to work on
the letters clothing lUGGAGe are the L and the E at its two ends, and that pair is what goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Luggage' is not a synonym for anything here - it is the word on the page, and the answer loses the two letters standing at its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a child by the plainest route there is: same sense, same stage of life, one word standing in for the other.

clue.text: Detective follows street maps of Mexican empire

indicators.note: what follows something comes along behind it, so this piece takes the later place

blocks.note: the A-Z is the book of street maps in every British glovebox
a tec is a detective in old slang

explanation.walkthrough: Two pieces of vocabulary worth keeping: 'tec' for a detective, and street maps for the A-Z rather than a range of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs ruled central Mexico until Cortes arrived, so the people's name is standing for the empire they built.

clue.text: Bears witness to cycling examination taken

indicators.note: a cycled word rolls its front letter round to the back, everything else keeping its order

blocks.note: an examination that has been taken has been sat
an examination is a test

explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are assembled first and spun afterwards: the S at the front of the pair rolls round to the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest a thing is to swear to it as a witness, which is what bearing witness to it means in a courtroom.

clue.text: Revealing Latvian spirit stocked by pub

indicators.note: a bar keeps its drink inside itself, so whatever stocks a thing has it within

blocks.note: a Lett is a Latvian
an inn is a pub, and it opens up after its second letter
go is spirit in the sense of drive - 'plenty of go'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like the drink a pub would stock and turns out to be pep, which is where the clue hides its joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to give a secret away, so 'Revealing' matches the phrase in sense and in its -ing ending both.

clue.text: No vehicle leaving with flowers

definitions.note: A nosegay is a single bunch, so the plural 'flowers' names what it is made of rather than agreeing with it in number.

indicators.note: whatever leaves is gone, so the letter named walks out of the word

blocks.note: the word is taken at face value, two letters
a Segway is the two-wheeled machine you ride standing up
w is the standard short form of with, and it is the letter that leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like joinery holding the sentence together and is really a letter to be taken away - the commonest trap in a deletion clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers carried in the hand, from the days when a nose wanted something sweet held under it.

clue.text: Fear agent's latest blunder

indicators.note: the latest thing is the one that arrived last, and in a word that is the final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of agenT
a blunder is an error

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as spy fiction; the wordplay wants one letter of the agent and the mistake he made, nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is fear at its sharpest, the same emotion named at full strength rather than a different one.

clue.text: Some detecting edits on the radio

indicators.note: a voice on the radio is heard and never seen, so you write down what the word sounds like

blocks.note: somebody who edits the objectionable out is a censor, and censors said aloud is what you write in

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that sound identical and share no work at all: one keeps things out of print, the other picks up heat and movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensors are the devices that detect light, heat or motion, so 'some detecting' names them by the one thing they do.

clue.text: Irish town house outside school erected

indicators.note: what stands outside a thing wraps round it, part in front and part behind
a thing erected has been stood on end, which in a down clue turns it bottom to top

blocks.note: ho. is the estate agent's short form of house
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is the whaling word rather than the classroom one, and spotting that is the step the whole clue turns on.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone, so the clue defines by example - one town in Ireland standing in for its name.

clue.text: Place similar to Britain without any Kings?

indicators.note: to be without a thing is to lack it, so every letter named is missing from what is left

blocks.note: one thing similar to another is like it
UK is Britain on the back of a car
K is king on a playing card, and both of the ones here are dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the liberty in 'any Kings': it means every K in sight, and there happens to be one in each half.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu of something is in place of it, so 'Place' is the sense the French loanword still carries in that phrase.

clue.text: Country concerned with Iran kidnapping leader of military while undergoing revolution

indicators.note: a kidnapper carries someone off and shuts them away, so the seized letter ends up in the middle
a revolution turns a thing right round, so the assembly is read the other way about

blocks.note: a book on birds is a book concerned with birds
the country named, which opens up before its last letter
the leading letter of Military
as means while - 'as I was walking'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Middle Eastern politics and the answer is a tiny republic inside Italy, reached only by reading the whole assembly backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a sovereign republic entirely surrounded by Italy, so 'Country' is the plain category its name belongs to.

clue.text: Crash parking Duster around November

indicators.note: what goes around a thing closes over it, leaving it stuck in the middle

blocks.note: P is the parking sign at the roadside
a duster is a rag
November is N in the radio alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter is a decoy - a Duster is a car you could well crash - but the clue only ever wanted the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To prang a car is to crash it, RAF slang for a smash that has stuck in British English ever since the war.

clue.text: Expected shots where young footballers might play kilometres away

definitions.note: Par is a single number, the strokes a hole should take, so the plural 'shots' names what is being counted rather than agreeing with the answer.

indicators.note: something away is not there, so the letter named is missing from what remains

blocks.note: a park is where a kickabout happens
k is the abbreviation for kilometre, and it is the letter that goes

explanation.walkthrough: Golf and football share one clue: the pitch is a park, and the distances on the road signs hand you the letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the number of strokes a good golfer needs for a hole, so the definition is the game's technical sense of the word.

clue.text: Perennial hosed gently drinks

indicators.note: whatever a thing drinks it takes right inside itself, which is where these letters are sitting

blocks.note: the answer runs across the join of hoSED GEntly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' is the gardener's noun rather than the adjective - a plant that comes back each year, and this one likes wet ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grassy marsh plant that returns year after year, which is what a gardener means by a perennial.

clue.text: Alien hunter lay camouflaged

indicators.note: camouflage hides a thing by breaking up its outline, and these letters have had theirs broken up

blocks.note: nine letters, exactly the length the answer asks for

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' is doing adjective duty here: not a creature at all, but the quality a noise has when it belongs nowhere on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unearthly is not of this earth, which is 'alien' used as an adjective - strange and other-worldly rather than a visitor.
